title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class mixed add/square rho on GT

claims.statement: For uniform z in GT and uniform nonidentity input (the challenge of rules.md), the algorithm in proof.md returns P with e(P, Q) = z with probability at least 0.39 (model 0.390001), using at most 2^125.700213 target-group-operation equivalents (score 125700213/1000000), including preprocessing (2^75.405357), the adder table, walk starts and restarts, distinguished-point storage, collision replay, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^73.153638 bytes. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Each walk step is one Fp12 multiplication (charged 1) or one cyclotomic squaring (kappa = 0.4902), plus c2 = 0.1409 units of other work, measured by Callgrind on the organizer's blst build. The bound rests on heuristics H1-H4 in proof.md. This is a classical generic attack, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the Frobenius-class mixed walk (cscore.gt) on toy order-ell subgroups of F_{q^12}^* with ell dividing q^4 - q^2 + 1, solve each instance end to end and verify g^y = z, and compare the success curve of tau = T^2 V / (2N) with 1 - exp(-tau), reporting cycle rates. Toy scale only: it tests H1 and the solver, not production cost.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters, the measured c2 and kappa, and cscore.exact.
